name: Muxin 0.8.1
body:
Muxin is a desktop app that puts all your computers in one window: Macs, Linux servers, Windows PCs and cloud machines. Run AI coding agents on them, see their screens and check their logs. Your AI agents can use it too.

A fix for 0.8.0's apps in windows of their own, on Windows machines.

## Fixed

- **A Windows app resized past its screen's edge.** Making an app's window bigger here could push the app there past the edge of its screen, and that part showed black. Now the app moves left and up just enough to stay on its screen. When you close its window here, it goes back where it was.

## Install

**Homebrew** (macOS and Linux): `brew install --cask lumarylabsllc/tap/muxin`

**macOS** (12 or later, Apple silicon or Intel): open `Muxin-0.8.1-macos.dmg` and drag Muxin to Applications. It's signed and notarized, so it opens without a warning.

**Linux** (glibc 2.35 or newer: Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36, openSUSE Tumbleweed, RHEL 10 and later), for Intel and AMD (`x86_64`) or Arm (`aarch64`):

- **Debian and Ubuntu:** `sudo apt install ./Muxin-0.8.1-linux-x86_64.deb`
- **Fedora, openSUSE and RHEL:** `sudo dnf install ./Muxin-0.8.1-linux-x86_64.rpm` (or `sudo zypper install`)
- **Arch:** `yay -S muxin-bin` from the AUR, or `sudo pacman -U Muxin-0.8.1-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`
- **Any distribution:** `Muxin-0.8.1-linux-x86_64.AppImage`. Make it executable and run it. It needs no FUSE 2.
- **Without root:** unpack `Muxin-0.8.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` and run `./Muxin/install.sh`. Run `./Muxin/install.sh --uninstall` to remove it.

Use `aarch64` in place of `x86_64` on Arm.

**Windows 11**: `Muxin-0.8.1-windows-x64-setup.exe` for Intel and AMD, or `Muxin-0.8.1-windows-arm64-setup.exe` for Windows on Arm. It installs for you, without administrator rights. The installer isn't signed yet, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC": click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. The `.zip` files have the same app, unpacked.

Muxin sets up its own small helper on each machine you add. Your machines only need `ssh` with a key. Boxes need Docker on the machine they run on.

## Check your download

`SHA256SUMS.txt` has each file's checksum:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing
```

name: Muxin 0.8.0
body:

This release opens one app from any of your machines in a window of its own, as if it ran on your computer: a Windows app on your Mac, for example. A machine's page has fewer buttons too.

## What's new

- **Apps in windows of their own.** Above a machine's desktop, **Apps** lists the apps open there (Windows, Macs, and Linux on X11). Pick one, and it opens here as a window of its own, at its size there.
  - Nothing of Muxin's goes around it. Drag the app's own title bar to move the window, and double-click it to zoom.
  - Click and type as usual. The app comes to the front there first, so your keys never land in another app.
  - Resize either window and the other follows. When you close it here, the app goes back to its size there. Minimize or quit the app there, and its window here does the same.
  - The pointer takes the app's shapes: a text cursor over text, a hand over links.
  - Text stays sharp: once the picture is still, it's sent again at full quality.
  - Close it with **⌘W** on a Mac, or **Ctrl+Shift+W** on Windows and Linux. A label says so the first few times. The app keeps running there.
  - It works even while other windows cover the app there. When nothing covers it, its menus and dialogs show too.
- **For your agents:** `muxin desktop windows <machine>` and the `desktop_windows` MCP tool list a machine's app windows. Pass `window:<id>` as the display to `desktop_screenshot` and `desktop_input` to see and use just one.
- **A machine's page has fewer buttons:** New session, Show desktop and Share; then **Logs | Services | Files**; then a refresh button and a **···** menu with **Install runner…** and **Remove** (or **Destroy** for cloud machines and VMs).

name: Muxin 0.7.0
body:
Muxin is a desktop app that puts all your computers in one window: Macs, Linux servers, Windows PCs and cloud machines. Run AI coding agents on them, see their screens and check their logs. Your AI agents can use it too.

This release brings Boxes: hand a task to an agent, and it works on it by itself in a container on one of your machines. You can also hand a session to another agent, or move it to another machine, with its work and a note of the conversation so far. The sidebar shows every machine on one line, and three new Terminal themes make Muxin look like an app in your terminal.

## What's new

- **Boxes.** A box is one task for an agent. It gets a container of its own on one of your machines, with a fresh checkout on a new branch, and its agent runs there with its permission prompts off. On the **Boxes** page (⌃3), click **New box**. Then pick:
  - **the code:** a repository on GitHub, or a folder on one of your machines. A folder's uncommitted changes and new files go along. The field suggests your repositories and checkouts as you type.
  - **the task**, the agent and the machine.

  The agent can push its branch and open a pull request with your GitHub login. A box pauses after 15 quiet minutes and picks up where it left off when you ask it more. Split a box's page (⌘D) for a shell in its container. The first box on a machine builds Muxin's image there, which takes a few minutes. Your agents can make boxes too, with the `box_create` MCP tool or `muxin box new`.
- **From a GitHub issue.** On an issue's page, **Hand off in a box** fills in New box from the issue: its repository, the task, and a branch named for it. The agent gets the issue's title and description, and opens a pull request that closes it. **Work on it with an agent** starts a session instead.
- **Hand off to another agent.** On a session's page, **Hand off** gives its work to another agent: start with Claude Code, go on with Codex. Muxin writes a note in the session's folder (`.muxin/handoff.md`): the git state, the agent's to-do list, and the conversation so far from the agent's own transcript. The new agent starts there and reads it. The old session ends, unless you keep it. A fresh session of the same agent works too, for a conversation that grew too long.
- **Move a session to another machine.** In the same menu, **Move to…** takes a session's work to another of your machines: its commits that aren't on GitHub yet, its uncommitted changes and its new files. They land on the same branch, in a worktree of a checkout there or a fresh clone. An agent picks up there with the note. The folder it left stays as it is. This works for git checkouts.
- **A new sidebar.** Each machine is one line, with its sessions, runners, containers and VMs in a tree under it. The runners line opens its runner, or lists them when there are several.
- **Terminal themes.** Terminal, Terminal Midnight and Terminal Paper draw Muxin like an app in your terminal: one monospace font, square corners, `[ Buttons ]` and `── Headings ──`. Pick one in **Settings › Appearance**, or with **Theme: Choose…** (⇧⌘P).
- **Agents' workspaces moved to Boxes.** The folders that AI tools you use elsewhere work in through Muxin are listed at the bottom of the Boxes page, and on each machine's page.
- **Text fields** get word and line editing: ⌥⌫ deletes a word, ⌘⌫ to the start, ⌥← and ⌥→ move by word, and ⌃A, ⌃E and ⌃K work as on a Mac. A double-click selects a word, and a triple-click everything.
- **Dialogs stay open** when you click beside them, so what you typed in one isn't lost.
- **Sessions:** typing into an agent that stopped reading its input no longer holds up the others. Answering a waiting Codex session works with its newer menus too.

## Install

**Homebrew** (macOS and Linux): `brew install --cask lumarylabsllc/tap/muxin`

- **Without root:** unpack `Muxin-0.7.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` and run `./Muxin/install.sh`. Run `./Muxin/install.sh --uninstall` to remove it.

Use `aarch64` in place of `x86_64` on Arm.

name: Muxin 0.6.0
body:
Muxin is a desktop app that puts all your computers in one window: Macs, Linux servers, Windows PCs and cloud machines. Run AI coding agents on them, see their screens and check their logs. Your AI agents can use it too.

This release lets you share a session, or a whole machine, by link. Whoever opens it joins from a browser, a phone or Muxin, and connects straight to your computer. You let each person in, and you decide what they can do.

## What's new

- **Share a session by link.** On a session's page, click **Share**. The link is made and copied, ready to paste into a chat. Whoever opens it joins from any browser, with nothing to install, or from Muxin. They watch. They type only if you let them. The share lasts an hour, or 15 minutes, 8 hours or a day.
- **Share a whole machine.** On a machine's page, **Share** gives guests its sessions, including ones started later. You can also share:
  - **its desktop**, to view, or to control for the people you choose. They pick the quality, from Low to Max.
  - **the web servers you pick.** They open at `localhost` on the guest's computer.
  - **starting and ending sessions.** Off unless you turn it on.

  Nothing else is shared: no files, no other ports, no shell of its own.
- **You let each person in.** When someone opens the link, a card shows their name and a 6-digit code. They see the same code. Ask them to read it out, then click **Let in**. The **Shared** button then shows who's there. From it you can let someone type or use the desktop, remove them, add an hour, or stop sharing.
- **Straight to your computer.** The two computers connect directly, encrypted end to end (WebRTC). The link's secret sits after the `#`, which browsers never send to a server. muxin.dev only passes two short messages so the computers can find each other. A relay carries the connection only when no direct path works, and it can't read it. See [how it stays secure](https://muxin.dev/docs/sharing#security).
- **Join from a phone or tablet.** The join page fits the screen. On a desktop you're let use, tap to click, touch and hold to right-click, drag with one finger, and scroll with two. A **Keyboard** button brings up your keyboard.
- **Shared machines sit in your sidebar.** A machine shared with you shows under **Shared with you** like one of your own, with its sessions, desktop and servers under it. Right-click any of them for what you can do there. To join, click **+** next to **Shared with you**, use **Machines › Join a Share…**, or paste the link into **Add a machine**.
- **Cut, Copy and Paste on right-click** in every text field.

Your computer hosts the share, so Muxin needs to be open and your computer awake while it lasts. The [Sharing docs](https://muxin.dev/docs/sharing) have the details.

name: Muxin 0.5.9
body:
Muxin is a desktop app that puts all your computers in one window: Macs, Linux servers, Windows PCs and cloud machines. Run AI coding agents on them, see their screens and check their logs. Your AI agents can use it too.

This release lets you open a machine's own Remote Desktop or Screen Sharing when nobody is signed in to it. It also fixes Windows runners, GitHub sign-in, and adding a machine under the wrong account. Most of it comes from your reports and pull requests.

## What's new

- **Open a machine with Remote Desktop or Screen Sharing.** When nobody is signed in to a machine, Show desktop has no screen to show. It used to try for about a minute first. Now it says so right away and offers the machine's own remote desktop, which shows the sign-in screen:
  - **Open with Remote Desktop** on Windows
  - **Open with Screen Sharing** on a Mac
  - **Open with RDP or VNC** on Linux

  It goes through Muxin's own connection to the machine, so it works away from home, and nothing has to be opened in a firewall. It's also in the machine's right-click menu, and on the command line as `muxin desktop rdp <machine>` and `muxin desktop vnc <machine>`. (#26)
- **Windows runners keep running.** Starting a runner that isn't a Windows service, or installing one that runs in the background, said it worked. But the runner stopped as soon as Muxin's connection to the machine closed. It now runs on its own, and Muxin tells you if it doesn't come up. (#22, #24)
- **Stopping a Windows runner signs it off from GitHub.** Muxin used to end the runner outright, and GitHub held on to its old session for a few minutes. A runner started again in that time stayed offline. Now Muxin asks the runner to stop, the way its own Windows service does, and the runner signs off from GitHub first.
- **Clear errors from Windows.** An error from Muxin's scripts on Windows used to show up as a block of `#< CLIXML` markup. It now reads as one sentence. Install logs also used to stop at "√ Connected to GitHub"; they now run to the end.
- **Muxin sees a GitHub sign-in right away.** Suppose you signed in to the GitHub CLI on a machine with no sessions open. Its Git card kept saying you weren't signed in, and setting up git there failed. Muxin now asks the machine again. (#23, #25)
- **Clear help when a machine doesn't know your account.** If you add a machine without an account name, Muxin signs in with the account name from this computer. When that account doesn't exist on the machine, Muxin used to suggest a command that couldn't work. The suggested command now names the account. If a Mac refuses that account, Muxin says so and tells you to add the machine as `name@host`.
- **Helper updates reach direct connections.** After Muxin updated its helper on a Windows machine, or on Linux without systemd, the direct connection kept using the old helper until the machine restarted. It now switches to the new one during the update.

Thanks to @nobody-ops for #24 and #25 and the reports behind them, and to @noorhshah96 for #26.

## Install

**Homebrew** (macOS and Linux): `brew install --cask lumarylabsllc/tap/muxin`

name: Muxin 0.5.8
body:
Muxin is a desktop app that puts all your computers in one window: Macs, Linux servers, Windows PCs and cloud machines. Run AI coding agents on them, see their screens and check their logs. Your AI agents can use it too.

This release has ten fixes, most of them from your reports and pull requests.

## What's new

- **Type Chinese in terminals.** With Pinyin or another input method, Muxin's terminals now go through it: what you're composing shows at the cursor, the candidate window opens there, and the finished text goes to the program. Before, your keys went straight to the program. (#5)
- **Code folders, in Settings.** Settings › General › Code folders lists where Muxin looks for your checkouts, and you can add your own, like `~/app`. Fix with agent and Review with agent then work in a worktree of your checkout, on its own branch, instead of a fresh clone. When they find no checkout, the dialog says where to add its folder. (#15)
- **Muxin finds the GitHub CLI on Windows machines.** A Windows machine's Git card always said the GitHub CLI wasn't installed, and didn't know git signs in with it. Signing in to GitHub there from Muxin works now too. (#21)
- **The shared clipboard keeps your newest copy.** When you shared the clipboard with a Linux desktop, a copy on your Mac could be replaced about a second later by an older one. Muxin no longer puts an older copy over a newer one. Text like é or 日本 now gets to and from a Mac intact, too. (#20)
- **Add a machine lists only computers.** With Tailscale's Mullvad add-on, it offered hundreds of Mullvad's VPN servers as machines to add, and Tailscale's hello.ts.net demo device. They're left out now. (#16)
- **Terminals on Macs keep letters like é.** When Muxin's helper on a Mac started without a language setting (for direct connections, or with Muxin opened from the Dock), so did its terminals: bash dropped an é as you typed it, and `ls` showed `?` for it. Terminals now get UTF-8 when they'd have no setting.
- **You can type / in text fields.** It jumped to Search instead, so you couldn't type a folder like `~/app` or a repository like `acme/api`.
- **Long folders fit in a session's header.** The folder goes onto its own line and wraps.
- **Safer helper updates.** Muxin sends its helper to each machine over ssh. If the connection dropped partway, the cut-off file replaced the working helper, and the machine had none until the next try. Now the new file has to match the build before it replaces anything.
- **Builds from source find their helper.** A Muxin built from source couldn't find the helper builds it installs on machines. It now uses its checkout's builds, or a helper built next to it with `cargo build --workspace`. (#18)

Thanks to @raylenzed (#5) and @spuder (#17, #19) for their pull requests, and to @spuder, @mihaijoldis, @fwends and @nobody-ops for their reports.

name: Muxin 0.5.7
body:
Muxin is a desktop app that puts all your computers in one window: Macs, Linux servers, Windows PCs and cloud machines. Run AI coding agents on them, see their screens and check their logs. Your AI agents can use it too.

## Security

This release fixes problems a security researcher reported privately. Please update, especially if you copy files between machines, sync workspaces, or use Windows machines.

- **Copying files only writes what you asked for.** Before, a compromised machine you copied from could add other files next to yours on the other machine. Links that point outside what you copy are now left out.
- **Pulling a workspace back no longer brings its `.git` folder.** A compromised workspace machine could have planted a command there that `git status` would run on your computer.
- **On Windows machines, a typographic quote can't break out.** A ’ in a prompt or command could end its quoting and run what followed.
- **Smaller fixes.**
  - Your GitHub token goes to a workspace only when GitHub says the repository is private.
  - Runner downloads are checked against GitHub's checksums, and runner tokens stay off command lines.
  - On Windows, runner folders can only be changed by administrators and you.
  - `muxin cloud login --token -` reads the token from standard input, so it stays out of your shell history.
  - Unpairing or removing a machine turns off only this app's direct connection.
  - On Windows machines, the direct connection answers only your local network and Tailscale.
  - `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` go only to github.com, and a GitHub Enterprise address must use https.
  - Muxin's files that hold tokens are private to you from the moment they're written.
  - Muxin installs its helper on your machines only from its own files, never from a folder above it.
  - The release pipeline is pinned and locked down.

Thanks to the security researcher who reported these privately.

## What changes for you

- **The shared clipboard is off until you turn it on,** in Settings › General › Clipboard. If you turned it on yourself before, it stays on. Copies from password managers aren't shared (except from the app on Linux, which can't tell them apart yet), and text a program in a terminal copies stays on your computer.
- **Workspace pulls bring files back, not commits.** Commit in your own checkout.

## What's new
